questions.question: The average height of 15 boys out of a class of 50 is 160 cm. If the average height of the remaining boys is 168 cm, the average height (in cm) of all the boys of the class is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of boys = 15 : 35 → **3 : 7**

Assume average height = **160 cm**

Deviation in second group = 168 − 160 = **+8 cm**

Net deviation for total parts (10) = 7 × 8 = **+56**

Average height = 160 + (56 ÷ 10) = 160 + 5.6 = **165.6 cm**

**∴ The correct answer is 165.6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of boys in first group (n₁) = **15**

Average height of first group (A₁) = **160 cm**

Total number of boys (N) = **50**

Average height of remaining boys (A₂) = **168 cm**

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a80e76dcb3a24a494b805d277a6f6b2db25ccb5a37704757b75b628281125eec.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total height of first 15 boys = 15 × 160 = **2400 cm**

⇒ Number of remaining boys = 50 − 15 = **35 boys**

⇒ Total height of 35 boys = 35 × 168 = **5880 cm**

⇒ Total height of all 50 boys = 2400 + 5880 = **8280 cm**

⇒ Average height of class = 8280 ÷ 50

⇒ Average height = **165.6 cm**

**∴ The correct answer is 165.6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

When groups with different averages are combined, the combined average is the total sum divided by the total count: Aₐvg = Σ (nᵢ × Aᵢ) ÷ Σ nᵢ.

Deviation Method (Change in Average)

If one group is considered as the base average, the overall average increases/decreases by the (net deviation) ÷ (total quantity).

Alligation Rule

questions.question: A number when increased by 57 (1)/(2)\% gives 378. The number is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

When a number is increased by 57 ¹/₂% (57.5%), it becomes 378.

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Original Number × (1 + Percentage Increase / 100)

**Calculation:**

Let the original number be X.

According to the formula:

378 = X × (1 + 57.5 / 100)

378 = X × 1.575

⇒ X = 378 / 1.575

⇒ X = 240

**The original number is 240.**

questions.question: Tejas gets double the amount in 11 years when invested at compound interest, compounded annually. In how many years will the amount become four times itself?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n** times in **T** years, it will become **nk** times in **k × T** years.

Given: The amount becomes **2 times** in **11 years**.

Target: The amount needs to become **4 times**, which is **2²** times.

Here, n = 2, T = 11, and k = 2.

∴ Time taken = 2 × 11 = 22 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Principal = P

Amount after 11 years = 2P

Rate of interest = r% (compounded annually)

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc38e9236ae6f9d2e5519929f1ae90c36fa43813cb7411b90ab2160f1b9ecade.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹¹

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹¹ --- (Equation 1)

Let the time taken to become 4 times be **T** years.

⇒ 4P = P(1 + r/100)T

⇒ 4 = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ 2² = (1 + r/100)T

Substitute the value of 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹¹]² = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ (1 + r/100)²² = (1 + r/100)T

Comparing the exponents:

⇒ T = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exponential Growth in CI

In Compound Interest, the amount grows geometrically. If it doubles in 11 years, it will quadruple (2×2) in 11+11=22 years, and become 8 times (2×2×2) in 11+11+11=33 years.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate doubling time: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate of Interest. This is used for mental calculations in finance.

Effective Annual Rate

When interest is compounded more than once a year, the effective rate is higher. Effective Rate = [1 + r/(100×n)]ⁿ − 1, where n is frequency of compounding.</p

questions.question: The Cornwallis Code, introduced in 1793, is known for _______.​

options.text: establishing uniform police and judiciary reforms
introducing English as the court language

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**establishing uniform police and judiciary reforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cornwallis Code, introduced in **1793**, marked a significant step in British administrative reforms in India.
 
• This code established **uniformity in police and judiciary systems**, laying the foundation for modern legal and administrative systems in India.
 
• It emphasized the separation of **revenue collection and judicial functions** to avoid conflicts of interest.
 
• District judges were made independent of the revenue administration, ensuring impartial judicial processes.
 
• The code also introduced **strict regulations for the conduct of officials**, aiming to curb corruption and inefficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Cornwallis**

 
 
• He served as the Governor-General of Bengal from **1786 to 1793**.
 
• Known as the "father of civil services in India," he introduced reforms to make administration more efficient and accountable.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Reforms under Cornwallis**
 
 
• The establishment of **civil and criminal courts** at different levels (district, provincial, and Sadar levels).
 
• District judges were appointed, and the concept of **rule of law** was strengthened.
 
 
 
• **Police Reforms**
 
 
• The police system was reorganized, and **thanas (police stations)** were established to maintain law and order.
 
• The officers were made accountable, and their powers were clearly defined.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Cornwallis Code**
 
 
• It laid the groundwork for the **Indian Penal Code** and the modern judicial system in India.
 
• The reforms also influenced subsequent British administrative practices in the country.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios would most effectively necessitate the use of a three-dimensional reference within an MS Excel formula

options.text: Applying conditional formatting to a range of data based on values in another worksheet within the same workbook
Creating a chart that visualizes data points sourced from several different workbooks
Calculating the average sales figures across multiple non-contiguous worksheets for the same product category
Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A three-dimensional (3D) reference in MS Excel is used to reference the same cell or range of cells across multiple worksheets within the same workbook.
 
• It is particularly useful for performing calculations (e.g., summing, averaging) that involve data stored in the same cell position across identically structured worksheets.
 
• The correct scenario here—"Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year"—requires referencing the same cell (e.g., B2) across worksheets such as "Jan," "Feb," "Mar," etc.
 
• An example of a 3D reference formula for summing cell B2 across worksheets "Jan" to "Dec" would be: =SUM(Jan:Dec!B2).
 
• This method simplifies complex calculations and avoids manually navigating to each worksheet, making it efficient for managing large datasets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **3D Reference in MS Excel**

 
 
• A 3D reference allows users to refer to the same range or cell across multiple worksheets.
 
• It is denoted by the syntax: Sheet1:SheetN!CellReference.
 
• Common functions used with 3D references include SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, and MIN.
 
 
 
• **Conditional Formatting vs. 3D References**
 
 
• Conditional formatting applies visual formatting rules to data within a single worksheet or across specific ranges, but it does not use 3D references.
 
• 3D references are designed for computations rather than formatting tasks.
 
 
 
• **Identically Structured Worksheets**
 
 
• These are worksheets that share the same layout, such as having the same rows, columns, and headings.
 
• Identical structure is a prerequisite for effectively using 3D references.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of 3D References**
 
 
• Enables efficient data analysis across multiple worksheets.
 
• Reduces redundancy by avoiding repetitive formulas for each worksheet.
 
• Improves consistency and minimizes human error in calculations.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of 3D References**
 
 
• 3D references cannot be used in array formulas or with certain Excel features like Data Tables.
 
• Deleting or rearranging worksheets within the referenced range may lead to formula errors.

questions.question: India's demographic profile on the eve of independence reflected the socio-economic backwardness caused by colonial rule. Which of the following options best describes the health care and literacy statistics on the eve of independence?

__
 
• Life expectancy at birth during India’s independence (1947) was estimated to be around **32 years**, which is considered extremely low compared to global standards.
 
• Birth rates and death rates were both **high**, indicative of poor healthcare infrastructure and lack of access to medical facilities.
 
• Infant mortality rates were alarming, with nearly **150-200 infant deaths per 1,000 live births**.

• Life expectancy serves as an indicator of the general health and living conditions in a country.
 
• India’s low life expectancy at independence reflected widespread poverty, malnutrition, and limited access to healthcare.
 
 
 
• **High Birth and Death Rates**
 
 
• High birth rates were driven by social and economic factors such as lack of contraception and the need for large families in agrarian societies.
 
• High death rates were caused by rampant diseases like malaria, cholera, and tuberculosis, compounded by poor sanitation and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Infant Mortality**
 
 
• Infant mortality refers to the death of children under one year of age per 1,000 live births.
 
• India’s high infant mortality rate at independence underscored the lack of maternal and child healthcare services.
 
 
 
• **Colonial Impact on Education**
 
 
• Colonial policies largely ignored mass education, focusing instead on creating a small class of elites for administrative purposes.
 
• The absence of widespread educational initiatives led to the low literacy rates observed at independence.
 
 
 
• **Post-Independence Reforms**
 
 
• After independence, India embarked on initiatives to improve healthcare and education, such as the establishment of primary schools and public health programs.
 
• These efforts contributed to gradual improvements in life expectancy and literacy rates over the decades.

questions.question: If A's salary is 12% more than that of B, then by what percentage is B's salary less than that of A (correct to two decimal places)

Use the direct percentage reduction formula: **[r / (100 + r)] × 100**

Here, r = 12%

Reduction = [12 / (100 + 12)] × 100

Reduction = [12 / 112] × 100 ≈ 10.71%

**∴ The correct answer is 10.71%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A’s salary is 12% more than B’s salary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31d409ac551a02eab2470cacaed017af82f1d753748a0bdce07a013c84a7cf93.png] 

⇒ Let **B’s salary** = 100

⇒ **A’s salary** = 100 + 12% of 100 = 112

⇒ **Difference** = 112 − 100 = 12

⇒ **Percentage by which B is less than A** = (12 / 112) × 100

⇒ 3/28 × 100 = 300 / 28 = 75 / 7

⇒ 10.7142...

**∴ The correct answer is 10.71%.**

Percentage Increase/Decrease

If A is R% more than B, then B is [R / (100 + R)] × 100% less than A.

Inverse Case

If A is R% less than B, then B is [R / (100 − R)] × 100% more than A.

Fraction Equivalents

12% = 3/25. If B is 25, A is 25+3=28. B is 3/28 less than A. 1/28 ≈ 3.57%, so 3/28 ≈ 10.71%.</p

questions.question: On a circular path of 2742 m, Riya and Trisha start walking from the same point but in opposite directions at the speed of 4.6 m/s and X m/s, respectively. They will meet for the first time after 457 seconds. Find the value of X.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 2742 m, Time = 457 seconds.

Relative speed = Distance ÷ Time = 2742 ÷ 457 = 6 m/s.

In opposite directions, Relative speed = Speed₁ + Speed₂.

6 = 4.6 + X ⇒ X = 6 − 4.6 = 1.4 m/s.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.4 m/s.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/866ea48e29784c60a720b71d3f7ecc80df5d65496a51a0099f7810e184c8404e.png] 

**Given:**

Length of circular path (D) = 2742 m

Speed of **Riya** (S₁) = 4.6 m/s

Speed of **Trisha** (S₂) = X m/s

Time taken to meet (T) = 457 s

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (opposite direction) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ 457 = 2742 ÷ (4.6 + X)

⇒ 4.6 + X = 2742 ÷ 457

⇒ 4.6 + X = 6

⇒ X = 6 − 4.6

⇒ X = 1.4 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 1.4 m/s.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Circular Motion

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If they move in the same direction, it is the difference |S₁ − S₂|.

First Meeting on a Circular Track

The time taken for the first meeting is given by T = L ÷ (S₁ ± S₂), where L is the length of the track.

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time taken to meet at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the times taken by each person to complete one full lap: LCM(L/S₁, L/S₂).</p

Calculate **Total Frequency (N)** = 11 + 16 + 14 + 29 + 40 + 21 + 17 = 148.

Find **Median Position** = N/2 = 148/2 = 74.

Identify **Median Class**: Cumulative frequencies are 11, 27, 41, 70, 110... Since 74 falls in the 110 group, the class is **60-70**.

Apply **Interpolation**: Median = 60 + [(74 − 70) / 40] × 10 = 60 + [4 / 40] × 10 = 60 + 1 = 61.

**Given:** Frequency distribution of **patients' ages**.

**Formula Used:** Median = l + [((N/2) − cfₚ) / f] × h

Where: l = lower limit of **median class**, N = total frequency, cfₚ = cumulative frequency of preceding class, f = frequency of median class, h = class width.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc84849d249331aaa1f35725d8f367b0c5c79f50add9a5da3ba79606303c51a8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Cumulative Frequencies (cf):**

20-30: 11

30-40: 11 + 16 = 27

40-50: 27 + 14 = 41

50-60: 41 + 29 = 70 (cfₚ)

60-70: 70 + 40 = 110 (Median Class)

70-80: 110 + 21 = 131

80-90: 131 + 17 = 148 (N)

⇒ N/2 = 148 / 2 = 74

⇒ **Median Class** is 60-70 because its cf (110) is just greater than 74.

⇒ l = 60, cfₚ = 70, f = 40, h = 10

⇒ Median = 60 + [(74 − 70) / 40] × 10

⇒ Median = 60 + [4 / 40] × 10

⇒ Median = 60 + [1 / 10] × 10

⇒ Median = 60 + 1 = 61

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is given by: **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

Median for Ungrouped Data

If n is odd, Median = ((n+1)/2)th term. If n is even, Median = Average of (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th terms.

Class Mark

The **Class Mark** (xᵢ) is the mid-value of a class interval: (Upper Limit + Lower Limit) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: A grocer marked his goods at 70% above the cost price and sold them at a discount of X%. If he gained 53% profit, then find the value of X

__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 70% of 100 = 170.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 53% of 100 = 153.

**Discount** = MP − SP = 170 − 153 = 17.

**Discount % (X)** = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (17 ÷ 170) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Markup %** = 70%, **Profit %** = 53%.

Formulas: 100 + Profit% = (100 + Markup%) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

⇒ 1530 = 17 × (100 − X)

⇒ 90 = 100 − X

⇒ X = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between MP and CP

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is given by MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Percentage Change

Profit% can be calculated using successive formula: Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup × Discount) ÷ 100.</p

questions.question: A manufacturer fixes his selling price at 30% over the cost of production. If the cost of production goes up by 30%, and the manufacturer raises his selling price by 70%, find the profit percentage.

questions.question: The LCM of 40, 78 and another number, X, is 7800. Which of the following can be the value of X.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**LCM** of **40, 78, and X** = 7800.

Prime factorization: 7800 = 2³ × 3¹ × 5² × 13¹.

Check options for **prime factors**: 200 = 2³ × 5². These factors are already within the **LCM** prime factorization.

Testing other options: 180 has 3², which exceeds 3¹ in the **LCM**; 127 and 152 have prime factors (127, 19) not present in 7800.

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 40, 78 and X. **LCM** = 7800.

**Formula Used:** **LCM** is the product of the **highest power** of all prime factors present in the numbers.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 40 = 2³ × 5¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 78 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 13¹

⇒ Prime factorization of **LCM** (7800) = 2³ × 3¹ × 5² × 13¹

⇒ Comparing **LCM** factors with 40 and 78, we see that the factor 5² is not fully satisfied (40 only has 5¹).

⇒ Therefore, **X** must contain 5² and its other prime factors must not exceed the powers in the **LCM**.

⇒ Checking Option (4): 200 = 2³ × 5². This fits perfectly as 5² is present and 2³ is within limits.

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is **divisible** by all the numbers in a set. It is found by taking the highest power of each prime factor.

HCF and LCM Relation

For two numbers a and b, **Product of numbers = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**.

Prime Factorization Method

Express each number as a product of **primes**. **LCM** includes every prime factor at its maximum observed exponent.</p

questions.question: Which of the following statements DOES NOT describe the primary difference between SRAM and DRAM in terms of their internal architecture and performance characteristics?

options.text: DRAM is much faster because it has a simple design and doesn’t need refresh.
DRAM uses one transistor + one capacitor (1T1C) per cell (high density), while SRAM uses multiple transistors per bit (lower density).
SRAM is faster and more expensive → used for CPU caches; DRAM is slower and cheaper → used for main memory (RAM).
SRAM uses more transistors per bit, yielding faster access than DRAM.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1) “DRAM is much faster and doesn’t need to refresh.”**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Why Option 1 is invalid:** *DRAM* is **slower** than SRAM and it **does require periodic refresh** to retain data. The statement reverses both facts.
 
• **Actual DRAM cell:** Typically **1 transistor + 1 capacitor (1T1C)** per bit → *high density, low cost*, but needs refresh → *higher latency* than SRAM.
 
• **Actual SRAM cell:** Typically **multiple transistors (≈6T)** forming a bistable latch → *no refresh needed, faster access*, but *lower density and higher cost*.
 
• **Common usage:** *SRAM* → CPU **caches** (L1/L2/L3). *DRAM* → system **main memory** (DIMMs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3 (Correct statement):** *SRAM* is faster and more expensive → used for **cache**; *DRAM* is slower and cheaper → used for **main memory**.
 
• **Option 4 (Correct statement):** SRAM’s multi-transistor latch enables **faster access** than DRAM’s capacitor-based cell.
 
• **Performance note:** Refresh operations and sense-amp charging in DRAM introduce extra delay; SRAM reads/writes directly from a stable latch.

questions.question: Which smallest number should be added to 22938 so that the sum is completely divisible by 7?
questions.solution:

Divide the given number **22938** by **7** to find the remainder.

22938 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of **6**.

The smallest number to be added = **7 − Remainder** = 7 − 6 = **1**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The number to be made divisible is **22938**.

The divisor is **7**.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number to be added = **Divisor − Remainder**

**Calculations:**

⇒ 22938 ÷ 7

⇒ 22938 = 7 × 3276 + 6

⇒ Remainder = **6**

⇒ Required smallest number to be added = 7 − 6

⇒ Required smallest number to be added = **1**

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

Divisibility Rule of 7

Double the last digit of the number and subtract it from the remaining number. If the result is divisible by 7, then the original number is also divisible by 7.

Smallest Number to Subtract

To make a number completely divisible by a divisor, the smallest number that should be subtracted is equal to the **Remainder** itself.

Smallest Number to Add

To make a number completely divisible by a divisor, the smallest number that should be added is equal to **(Divisor − Remainder)**.</p

questions.question: If x2 + y2 − 10x + 26y + 194 = 0, then the value of x2 + y2 is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify half of the coefficients of **x** and **y**: **a = 10/2 = 5** and **b = 26/2 = 13**.

Check if **a² + b²** equals the constant: **5² + 13² = 25 + 169 = 194**.

Since the sum matches, the equation is **(x − 5)² + (y + 13)² = 0**.

This directly gives **x = 5** and **y = −13**.

Calculating **x² + y² = 5² + (−13)² = 194**.

**∴ The correct answer is 194.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x² + y² − 10x + 26y + 194 = 0

**Formula Used:** (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² and (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

⇒ Group the terms: (x² − 10x) + (y² + 26y) + 194 = 0

⇒ Complete the square for **x**: (x² − 2 × 5 × x + 5²) − 25

⇒ Complete the square for **y**: (y² + 2 × 13 × y + 13²) − 169

⇒ Substitute back: (x − 5)² − 25 + (y + 13)² − 169 + 194 = 0

⇒ (x − 5)² + (y + 13)² − 194 + 194 = 0

⇒ (x − 5)² + (y + 13)² = 0

⇒ Since the sum of squares of real numbers is zero, each term must be zero.

⇒ **x − 5 = 0** ⇒ **x = 5**

⇒ **y + 13 = 0** ⇒ **y = −13**

⇒ Value of **x² + y² = 5² + (−13)²**

⇒ 25 + 169 = 194

**∴ The correct answer is 194.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Property

If the sum of squares of multiple real expressions is zero, i.e., **A² + B² + C² = 0**, then **A = 0, B = 0, and C = 0** individually.

Perfect Square Trinomial

A quadratic expression **ax² + bx + c** is a perfect square if its discriminant **D = b² − 4ac = 0**.

Completing the Square Technique

To make **x² + bx** a perfect square, we add and subtract **(b/2)²**, resulting in **(x + b/2)² − (b/2)²**.</p

questions.question: Find the value of K, for which the quadratic equation x2 + 4x + K=0 have equal roots?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For any **quadratic equation** of the form x² + bx + K = 0, the condition for **equal roots** is K = (b/2)².

In the given equation x² + 4x + K = 0, the value of b is 4.

Substituting the value: K = (4 ÷ 2)² = 2² = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The **quadratic equation** is x² + 4x + K = 0.

**Formula Used:** For a standard **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots are **equal** if and only if the **discriminant** (D) is zero.

The formula for the **discriminant** is D = b² − 4ac.

⇒ Comparing x² + 4x + K = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we get:

⇒ a = 1, b = 4, c = K

⇒ For **equal roots**, D = 0

⇒ (4)² − 4 × 1 × K = 0

⇒ 16 − 4K = 0

⇒ 4K = 16

⇒ K = 16 ÷ 4

⇒ K = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

The value of D = b² − 4ac determines the nature of roots: D > 0 means real and distinct roots, D = 0 means **real and equal roots**, and D < 0 means **imaginary roots**.

Sum and Product of Roots

For the equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the **Sum of roots** (α + β) = −b/a and the **Product of roots** (αβ) = c/a.

Quadratic Formula

The roots of a **quadratic equation** are calculated using x = (−b ± √D) ÷ 2a.</p

Height of **isosceles triangle** (h) = √(a² − (b/2)²) where a = 41 and b = 18.

h = √(41² − 9²) = √(1681 − 81) = √1600 = 40 cm.

Area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 18 × 40 = 360 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 360 cm².**

⇒ Height² + (Base/2)² = (Equal side)²

⇒ h² + 9² = 41²

⇒ h² + 81 = 1681

⇒ h² = 1600

⇒ h = 40 cm

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150.

To gain 8%, **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 8% of 100 = 108.

**Discount** = MP − SP = 150 − 108 = 42.

**Discount%** = (42 ÷ 150) × 100 = 28%.

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Markup% = 50%, Profit% = 8%.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2dd260efb35a3ce578a325b50808ae87e5a25518a8cdcd29429d4388cfa25edc.png] 
⇒ Assume **CP** = 100.
⇒ **MP** = 100 × (150 ÷ 100) = 150.
⇒ **SP** = 100 × (108 ÷ 100) = 108.
⇒ **Discount Amount** = 150 − 108 = 42.
⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (42 ÷ 150) × 100 = 28%.

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup and Discount Relation

The relation between CP and MP is given by: **CP ÷ MP = (100 − D%) ÷ (100 + P%)**.

Effective Percentage Change

Profit% can also be calculated as: **Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup × Discount) ÷ 100**.</p

questions.question: The median of the observations 54, 65, 77, 34, 68, 66, 60, 70, 33, 71 and 15 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given **11 observations** in **ascending order**:

15, 33, 34, 54, 60, **65**, 66, 68, 70, 71, 77

Since the number of terms (N = 11) is **odd**, the **median** is the middle term:

Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term = 6th term = **65**

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Observations: 54, 65, 77, 34, 68, 66, 60, 70, 33, 71, 15

Total number of observations (N) = **11**

**Formula Used:**

When N is odd, Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term of the sorted data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d55ade4cdb5c7e01df5b0f7265314b09ce1e8eec6a3085e7d989d3706465a2c0.png] 

**Calculations:**

First, arrange the given observations in **ascending order**:

⇒ 15, 33, 34, 54, 60, 65, 66, 68, 70, 71, 77

Count the number of observations (N):

⇒ N = 11

Since N is an **odd number**, the median is calculated as:

⇒ Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = (12 ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = 6th term

Looking at the sorted list, the 6th term is **65**.

Let us verify why the other options are incorrect:

⇒ Option (1) 68 is the 8th term, which is not the middle term.

⇒ Option (3) 66 is the 7th term, which is not the middle term.

⇒ Option (4) 61 is not present in the given set of observations.

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If the number of observations (N) is even, the median is the average of the (N ÷ 2)th term and the ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th term after sorting.

Mean vs Median vs Mode

Mean is the average of all values. Median is the middle value. Mode is the most frequently occurring value in the dataset.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary objective of the Sagarmala Project by the Ministry of Shipping?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Sharad can complete a piece of work alone in 13 days and Varad can complete the same piece of work alone in 9 days. They started the work together, but Varad had to leave 11 days before the completion of the work. In how many days will the work complete?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 13 and 9) = 117 units.

If a person leaves **before completion**, add their potential work to the total.

Total units = 117 + (Varad's efficiency × days before completion) = 117 + (13 × 11) = 117 + 143 = 260 units.

Total days = Adjusted Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 260 ÷ (9 + 13) = 260 ÷ 22 = 130 ÷ 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11(9/11) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sharad takes 13 days, Varad takes 9 days. Varad leaves 11 days before completion.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **Sharad**

 **Varad**
 9

⇒ Let the total work be completed in **x days**.

⇒ Sharad worked for **x days** and Varad worked for **(x − 11) days**.

⇒ 9 × x + 13 × (x − 11) = 117

⇒ 9x + 13x − 143 = 117

⇒ 22x = 117 + 143

⇒ 22x = 260

⇒ x = 260 ÷ 22 = 130 ÷ 11 = 11(9/11)

**∴ The correct answer is 11(9/11) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leaving Before Completion

When a person leaves **n days** before completion, treat it as if they worked those **n days** by adding their work to the total LCM.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. If time ratio is A:B, the efficiency ratio is B:A.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is identical to work; however, **outlet pipes** have negative efficiency while **inlet pipes** have positive efficiency.</p

questions.question: A man has to cover a distance of 387 km in 18 hours. If he covers two-third of this distance in 6/9 of the time, then what should his speed (in km/hr) be to cover the remaining distance in the time left?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Remaining distance** = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 of total = 387 ÷ 3 = 129 km.

**Remaining time** = 1 − 6/9 = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 of total = 18 ÷ 3 = 6 hours.

**Required Speed** = Remaining Distance ÷ Remaining Time = 129 ÷ 6 = 21.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 21.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2dc362807c7790581b97ffc3b5cc93a40ec7f27843266522483fc5fc887922e0.png] 
**Given:**

Total distance = **387 km**

Total time = **18 hours**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered = 387 × (2/3) = 258 km

⇒ Remaining distance = 387 − 258 = **129 km**

⇒ Time spent = 18 × (6/9) = 18 × (2/3) = 12 hours

⇒ Remaining time = 18 − 12 = **6 hours**

⇒ Required Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 129 ÷ 6

⇒ Required Speed = **21.5 km/hr**

**∴ The correct answer is 21.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed Formula

Speed is defined as the distance covered per unit of time. Formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. It is not always the arithmetic mean of individual speeds.</p

questions.question: What are the units for base quantities called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental or base units**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Base quantities are physical quantities that are defined independently and are used as the foundation for other derived quantities.
 
• The units for these base quantities are known as **fundamental or base units**.
 
• Examples of base units include the meter (m) for length, kilogram (kg) for mass, and second (s) for time.
 
• The **International System of Units (SI)** is the globally accepted standard that defines these fundamental units.
 
• The SI system includes seven base units, which are used worldwide for scientific and technical purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Base Quantities:**

 
 
• These are quantities like length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.
 
• They are considered independent and form the foundation of the measurement system.
 
 
 
• **SI Base Units:**
 
 
• The seven SI base units are: meter (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol), and candela (cd).
 
• Each unit corresponds to one of the seven base quantities.
 
 
 
• **Derived Units:**
 
 
• Derived units are formed by combining base units according to the relationships between physical quantities.
 
• Examples include the newton (N) for force and the joule (J) for energy.
 
 
 
• **History of SI Units:**
 
 
• The SI system was officially adopted in 1960 at the 11th General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM).
 
• It has since become the most widely used measurement system globally.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Standard Units:**
 
 
• Standardized units ensure consistency and comparability in measurements across different regions and disciplines.
 
• They are crucial for scientific research, trade, and technological development.
